h: The Leaves and Fruit of the Tree of Life

p: בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, חֵלֶק ג קעג, א)
In the holy Zohar (on this parshah, Zohar III 173a):
כַּד מְקַדְּשִׁין יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹמָא לְתַתָּא וְכוּלֵּי
when Yisrael sanctify the day below…" and so on;
then the Tree of Life is aroused
and knocks upon its leaves…" and so on;
"and the fragrances of the World to Come rise;
is aroused and brings forth holy souls…" and so on;
"and then all of Yisrael are crowned…" and so on.
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (חוּלִּין צב, א)
according to what they said in the Gemara (Chullin 92a)
about Yisrael, who were likened to a vine:
are the amei ha'aretz…" and so on;
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
And this is what the holy Zohar cited above says:
that the Tree of Life too
and from the leaves, called "its leaves,"
rise "the fragrances of the World to Come,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה יא, ג)
in the manner of what it says (Yeshayahu 11:3):
"And he shall be imbued with the fear of Hashem";
for fragrance alludes to fear of Heaven;
"Purity took away taste and fragrance…" and so on;
"I smell a fragrance…" and so on;
"My son, there is purity in you";
And in the Yerushalmi (beginning of chapter 4 of Demai):
"The awe of Shabbos is upon the am ha'aretz";
has the awe of Shabbos upon him.
And this is what it says, "its leaves":
raise the fragrance of the World to Come;
and this is at the onset of Shabbos,
attains fear of Heaven from the holiness of Shabbos.
"is aroused and brings forth holy souls";
which is "the soul of man is the lamp of Hashem";
"Your word is a lamp to my feet"
and this is for the talmidei chachamim.
who is called an apple tree,
"Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest,
so is my beloved among the young men."
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב ס, ב) אִיתָא
And in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 60b) it is stated:
וְאֵין עֵץ אֶלָּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
"And 'tree' means only HaKadosh Baruch Hu…" and so on;
this is the tree of the field of holy apples."
And the fruits of the tree
are the souls of the tzaddikim,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א פה, ב)
as is written in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 85b):
"'And his fruit is sweet to my palate':
these are the souls of the tzaddikim,
דְּכֻלְּהוּ אִיבָּא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
all of whom are the fruit of HaKadosh Baruch Hu…" and so on;

p: עַל הַפָּסוּק כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר וְגוֹ׳
on the pasuk "Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest…":
"Why were Yisrael likened to an apple tree?
put 'we will do' before 'we will hear.'"
which are the souls of the tzaddikim,
who fulfill the mitzvos and the words of Torah;
and "we will hear" is the leaves,
which is the aspect of fear of Heaven,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים ו, ד)
in the manner of what it says (Devarim 6:4):
for when one takes to heart
that the King of the kings of kings,
stands over him and sees his deeds,
fear of Heaven immediately comes to him,
as is written (in the Rema at the beginning of Orach Chaim).
And to this even amei ha'aretz attain,
why the Gemara did not bring the pasuk
דְּוְרֵיחַ אַפֵּךְ כַּתַּפּוּחִים (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ז, ט)
"and the fragrance of your nose like apples" (Shir HaShirim 7:9).
for about this it says "the fragrance of your nose,"
this is the fluid of a person's nose";
הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּרָא הָאָדָם הַזֶּה
and placed his drain at his entrance,
that pours out waste water and foul water.
"and the fragrance of your nose like apples,"
in the manner of what Chazal said
וַיָּרַח אֶת רֵיחַ בְּגָדָיו (בְּרֵאשִׁית כז, כז)
"'And he smelled the fragrance of his garments' (Bereishis 27:27):
that is, the lowliest in Yisrael.
"See, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a field,"
which is the field of Chakal Tapuchin;
but only with the kaf of comparison,
for it is not actually the fragrance of the field of apples,
in the manner of what is said
"'As an enemy,' but not an enemy…" and so on;
"'like a widow,' but not a widow";
and so it is in the Gemara (Taanis 20a).
the tree of good and evil,
out of the tree of good and evil, too,
And there is a lower teshuvah,
as is written in the holy Zohar
that after one repents of his sins
and goes on the path of a mitzvah,
and this is like Yosef Meshisa
and this is the meaning of
"goes on the path of a mitzvah."
And this is what it says,
"And he smelled the fragrance of his garments"
"like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed,"
which is a field of apples,
and they correspond to the leaves of the vine,
of the tree of good and evil,
and they merited to make it
And there is a higher teshuvah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
as the Ra'aya Mehemna cited above says:
who, after he regrets his sins,
with fear and love… and so on
this one merits the letter Vav.
And this corresponds to the clusters of the vine,
so that out of the tree of good and evil there is made,
"Why were Yisrael likened to an apple tree…,"
speaks of the Tree of Life,
which is the tree of the field of apples,
"and his fruit is sweet to my palate":
these are the souls of the tzaddikim.
And there are also the leaves,
which give off the fragrance of the World to Come;
that at the time of the giving of the Torah
Yisrael were likened to an apple tree,
for they put the fruits before the leaves,
"Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest,
and his fruit is sweet to my palate,"
which are the souls of the tzaddikim,
which are the fruits of the Tree of Life,
and there are also leaves of the Tree of Life,
which raises the fragrances of the World to Come.
"The awe of Shabbos is upon the am ha'aretz,"
And at the time of the giving of the Torah
in that they were likened to an actual apple tree,
and put "we will do" before "we will hear":

Two Levels of Teshuvah in the Vine

paragraphs.text: Source: Taanis 20a — “״היתה כאלמנה״, אמר רב יהודה, לברכה: כאלמנה — ולא אלמנה ממש, אלא כאשה שהלך בעלה למדינת הים, ודעתו לחזור עליה.” — “Similarly, with regard to the verse: “How she has become like a widow” (Lamentations 1:1), Rav Yehuda said: This too is for a blessing. The verse states that Jerusalem is like a widow, but is not an actual widow. Rather, Jerusalem is like a woman whose husband has gone to a country overseas. Without her husband by her side she is likened to a widow, and yet he intends to return to her.”
